messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: How to pass an argument to a mapreducer?
parts:
Change to
 y <- random(1:10,1)
    map.test <- as.expression(bquote({
      y = .(y)
      lapply(seq_along(map.values), function(r) {
        v <- map.values[[r]]
        k <- map.keys[[r]]
        rhcollect(k,v^y)
      })
    }))
 
 
 
Check out the ?bquote .  Stands for "backquote".  I learned of it here, but I have found it a very handy function.
 
 

On Thursday, June 28, 2012 2:58:44 AM UTC-7, rmx wrote:
Hello,

Imagine that I have a map to make a simple calculation with a y. The value of y is obtained in run time has in this dummy example: 
 
  y < random(1:10,1)
    map.test <- expression({
      lapply(seq_along(map.values), function(r) {
        v <- map.values[[r]]
        k <- map.keys[[r]]
        rhcollect(k,v^y)
      })
    })
    z <- rhmr(map=map.test, 
              ifolder=ifolder, 
              ofolder=ofolder, 
              inout=c("sequence", "sequence"),
              mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=4)
    )
    rhex(z)
  
In this example I will get an error because the value of y is not passed to the mapreduce. How can I pass it?

Thank you!
Rui

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] How to pass an argument to a mapreducer?
parts:
By end of day, rhipe 0.68 will be out.
in that case, for code would look like


y < random(1:10,1)
map.test <- rhmap({
## r is defined as map.values[[.index]] where .index runs from 1 ...
length(map.values)
rhcollect(k,r^y)
})
z <- rhwtach(rhmr(map=map.test,ifolder=ifolder,ofolder=ofolder,
param=list(y=y),
mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=4)),read=FALSE)


I'll post a message to this list by end of day (US EDT)
Saptarshi

use substitute (bquote is written using substitute).
The first two use it to remove boring boilerplate.
